engFgUs: Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. Wearing a tracksuit to the formal gala was a real ___. (a social blunder)
A faux pas is an embarrassing social mistake, like dressing wrongly for a formal event.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. Many residents wanted change, but the council preferred to keep the ___. (the existing state of affairs)
Status quo means the way things currently are.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. "Life is short," the coach said. "___ — go for the scholarship now." (seize the day)
Carpe diem is Latin for "seize the day," urging action now.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. Although English is the official language, Spanish is the ___ language of the neighbourhood. (in fact, though not officially)
De facto describes something that exists in practice even if not by law.

Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. After the championship, the star player felt a sense of ___, as if he had played this game before. (feeling of having already experienced something)
Déjà vu is the feeling that a new situation has happened before.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. Her ___ was contagious; she laughed and danced through every family reunion. (zest for life)
Joie de vivre means a cheerful enjoyment of life.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. The minister admitted the error at the press conference, saying simply, "___." (my fault)
Mea culpa is Latin for "my fault," an admission of guilt.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. Before boarding, her friends hugged her and shouted, "___!" (have a good trip)
Bon voyage is French for "have a good journey."
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. When his sister pointed out the flaw in his argument, he grinned and said, "___." (you have scored a point)
Touché acknowledges that someone has made a clever, valid point against you.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. The final goal in overtime was the ___ that ended the rival team's hopes. (a final decisive blow)
A coup de grâce is a final blow that finishes something off.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. The two leaders met for a private ___ before the summit. (a private conversation between two people)
A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. Music was her ___; she could not imagine life without it. (reason for existing)
Raison d'être means the most important reason for someone's existence.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. He showed real ___ in calming the angry customer. (skill in handling social situations)
Savoir-faire is the ability to act appropriately and smoothly in social situations.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. The meeting had no agenda, so members spoke ___. (without preparation)
Ad lib means spontaneously, without preparation.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. The novelist's latest book is considered her ___, the finest work of her career. (masterpiece)
Magnum opus refers to an artist's greatest work.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. Detectives noticed that every break-in followed the same ___. (method of operating)
Modus operandi is a characteristic way of doing something, often used about criminals.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. The summer camp built a strong ___ among the counsellors. (team spirit)
Esprit de corps is the shared pride and loyalty of a group.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. After the scandal, the senator offered a public ___ explaining his decisions. (a formal defence of one's actions)
An apologia is a formal written or spoken defence or explanation of one's actions.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. The archaeologists photographed the pottery ___ before moving it. (in its original place)
In situ means in the original position or place.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. Canada's spending on health care is high when measured ___. (per person)
Per capita means for each person, a common way to compare countries.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. The principal discussed the school's budget ___ the provincial guidelines. (in relation to)
Vis-à-vis means in relation to or compared with.
Choose the expression that best completes the sentence. He repeated the same story ___ until everyone left the room. (to a sickening degree)
Ad nauseam means repeated so often that it becomes tiresome.
engNuCd: Choose the best word. The ___ old house had stood empty for decades, its windows broken. (negative: neglected)
Decrepit suggests something worn out and falling apart, a negative connotation.
Choose the best word. My grandmother is very ___; she saves every bit of string and reuses jars. (positive: careful with money)
Thrifty means careful with money and has a positive connotation, unlike stingy or miserly.
Choose the best word. The ___ puppy bounced around the yard, delighting the children. (positive: lively)
Spirited means full of energy in a positive way.
Choose the best word. The politician gave a ___ answer to avoid admitting anything. (negative: deliberately unclear)
Evasive suggests dodging the truth, which is negative; diplomatic and tactful are positive.
Choose the best word. The hikers admired the ___ mountain peaks. (positive: impressive)
Majestic conveys grandeur and admiration, a positive connotation.
Choose the best word. He was so ___ that he refused to change his mind even when shown the evidence. (negative: unreasonably firm)
Pig-headed means stubborn in a negative way, while determined and resolute are positive.
Choose the best word. The new student was ___, preferring to listen before speaking. (neutral to positive: quiet)
Reserved describes quietness without the negative judgment of sullen or aloof.
Choose the best word. The crowd ___ through the gates, pushing and shoving. (negative: moved in a disorderly way)
Stampeded suggests a wild, uncontrolled rush, fitting the pushing and shoving.
Choose the best word. The scientist was ___ about checking every measurement twice. (positive: very careful)
Meticulous praises careful attention to detail, while fussy and nitpicky are negative.
Choose the best word. The salesperson's ___ grin made the customers distrust him. (negative: insincere)
A smirk is a smug, insincere smile, which explains the distrust.
Choose the best word. After the long winter, the garden had a ___ scent of lilacs. (positive: pleasant smell)
Fragrant describes a pleasant smell; pungent, reeking and musty suggest unpleasant ones.
Choose the best word. The ___ child asked endless questions about how the universe works. (positive: eager to learn)
Inquisitive suggests healthy curiosity, while nosy and prying are negative.
Choose the best word. Critics called the film's ending ___, saying it relied on cheap tears. (negative: overly emotional)
Mawkish means sentimental in an exaggerated, negative way.
Choose the best word. The volunteers were ___ in their support for the food bank. (positive: loyal and unwavering)
Steadfast describes firm loyalty positively, unlike obstinate or rigid.
Choose the best word. The rich landlord ___ the tenants' complaints. (negative: dismissed with contempt)
Scoffed at means mocked or dismissed with scorn, a negative action.
Choose the best word. The athlete was ___ after winning gold. (positive: proud and happy)
Elated means joyful without the negative self-importance of smug or conceited.
Choose the best word. The documentary showed the ___ conditions in the abandoned factory. (negative: dirty and unpleasant)
Squalid means filthy and wretched, clearly negative.
Choose the best word. The mayor's ___ speech inspired the crowd to volunteer. (positive: stirring)
Rousing means inspiring in a positive sense, while inflammatory suggests stirring up anger.
Choose the best word. He ___ his way to the front of the line, ignoring everyone else. (negative: pushed rudely)
Elbowed suggests rudely pushing past others, matching the negative tone.
Choose the best word. The ___ dog barked at every passer-by. (negative: hostile)
Vicious suggests dangerous aggression, a negative connotation.
Choose the best word. Her ___ outfit drew compliments at the party. (positive: fashionable)
Stylish is a compliment, while gaudy, flashy and garish criticize an outfit.
Choose the best word. The ___ bureaucrat insisted on three more forms for no reason. (negative: obsessed with petty rules)
Officious describes someone who enforces petty rules in an annoying way.
engNuPr: Which word fits the meaning best? The witness gave a ___ account of the accident, leaving out no detail. (complete and thorough)
Comprehensive means including everything, matching "leaving out no detail."
Which word fits the meaning best? The medicine ___ her pain within minutes. (made less intense)
Alleviated means made a pain or problem less severe.
Which word fits the meaning best? The two reports ___ each other, so investigators did not know which to believe. (disagreed with)
Contradicted means stated the opposite, explaining the confusion.
Which word fits the meaning best? The forest fire ___ thousands of hectares in northern Alberta. (destroyed by burning)
Consumed, used of fire, means burned up or destroyed.
Which word fits the meaning best? Her ___ to the cause never wavered, even in hard times. (loyal dedication)
Which word fits the meaning best? The professor's lecture was so ___ that few students could follow it. (difficult to understand)
Abstruse means hard to understand, explaining why few could follow.
Which word fits the meaning best? The crowd grew ___ as the delayed concert still had not started. (impatient and restless)
Which word fits the meaning best? The new evidence ___ the accused man, proving he was elsewhere. (cleared of blame)
Exonerated means officially cleared of blame.
Which word fits the meaning best? The two rivers ___ just east of the town. (flow together)
Converge means come together at a point.
Which word fits the meaning best? His ___ about the dangers of the ice saved lives that winter. (warning in advance)
Foresight is the ability to anticipate future problems.
Which word fits the meaning best? The report was criticized for its ___, using many words to say little. (wordiness)
Verbosity means using more words than necessary.
Which word fits the meaning best? She felt ___ about moving: excited for the new job but sad to leave friends. (having mixed feelings)
Ambivalent means having mixed or conflicting feelings.
Which word fits the meaning best? The sudden storm ___ the outdoor ceremony. (interrupted and threw into disorder)
Disrupted means interrupted or thrown into disorder.
Which word fits the meaning best? The judge remained ___, favouring neither side. (fair and unbiased)
Impartial means not favouring either side.
Which word fits the meaning best? A thick fog ___ the harbour, hiding every ship. (covered and hid)
Shrouded means covered so as to hide from view.
Which word fits the meaning best? The company's profits ___ after the scandal, falling sharply. (dropped suddenly)
Plummeted means fell steeply and quickly.
Which word fits the meaning best? The coach ___ the players for their hard work. (praised highly)
Which word fits the meaning best? The tiny cabin was ___ but comfortable. (small and plain)
Modest means small and simple rather than grand.
Which word fits the meaning best? The hikers had to ___ their water because the spring had dried up. (use sparingly)
Ration means limit use so a supply lasts.
Which word fits the meaning best? The speaker's ___ voice carried to the back of the hall. (loud and full)
Resonant describes a deep, full sound that carries.
Which word fits the meaning best? The plan was ___; nobody could see how it would ever work. (not practical)
Unfeasible means impossible or impractical to carry out.
Which word fits the meaning best? The diplomat tried to ___ the dispute before it turned into war. (calm and settle)
Defuse means reduce tension in a dangerous situation.
engNuTh: Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The tired runners collapsed at the finish line.
Exhausted means extremely tired, keeping the same meaning.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The professor is a famous expert on glaciers.
Renowned means famous and widely known.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? His rude comment upset the host.
Impolite is a synonym for rude.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The museum displayed a rare stamp from 1851.
Scarce means hard to find, the same as rare.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The detective found a hidden door behind the bookcase.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The team was happy after the victory.
Jubilant means joyful, especially after success.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The instructions were confusing.
Baffling means hard to understand, the same as confusing.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? She gave a generous donation to the hospital.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The old bridge looked dangerous.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The students were eager to start the experiment.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The wind was fierce on the prairie that night.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? He tried to persuade his parents to let him go.
Convince means persuade someone to agree.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The movie's ending was sad.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The town's population began to increase.
Grow means increase in size or number.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The singer had a unique style.
Distinctive means one of a kind, like unique.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The teacher was angry about the cheating.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The scientist made an important discovery.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The path through the woods was narrow.
Slim can mean narrow, as in a slim path.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The baby was sleepy after lunch.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The lake was still at dawn.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? Her answer was correct.
Accurate means correct and free of errors.
Which word can replace the word in bold without changing the meaning? The villain had a wicked plan.
Sinister means evil or threatening, like wicked.
engNuCt: Irregardless combines a negative prefix and suffix and is traditionally considered nonstandard.
Traditionalists hold that hopefully means "in a hopeful manner," though "it is to be hoped" is now widely accepted.
Bemused traditionally means confused, though many now use it to mean amused.
Peruse traditionally means to examine closely, though it is often used to mean skim.
Fortuitous traditionally means accidental, though it is now often used to mean lucky.
to weaken or drain of energy
Enervate means to weaken, despite often being mistaken for energize.
"The country comprises ten provinces and three territories."
"The country is comprised by ten provinces."
Traditionally, the whole comprises the parts, with no "of."
assumes the conclusion in the argument itself
Begging the question is traditionally a logical fallacy of circular reasoning, though many use it to mean "raises the question."
Anxious traditionally means worried; using it to mean eager is a newer, contested usage.
Reticent traditionally means reserved in speech, though it is often used to mean reluctant in general.
Presently traditionally means "soon," though "currently" is now common.
Momentarily traditionally means "for a brief time," though North Americans often use it to mean "very soon."
Which usage of whose and who's is correct?
"Who's coming, and whose coat is this?"
"Whose coming, and who's coat is this?"
"Who's coming, and who's coat is this?"
"Whose coming, and whose coat is this?"
Who's means "who is"; whose shows possession.
"We need less sugar in this recipe."
"We need less eggs in this recipe."
"There were less people at the game."
Less is traditionally used with uncountable nouns like sugar; fewer is used with countable nouns.
Traditionally, they as a singular pronoun is …
contested by some, but widely accepted for an unknown or non-binary person
always incorrect in any style guide
Singular they has a long history and is now accepted by most major style guides, though some still contest it.
Traditionally, impact as a verb ("The rules impact students") is …
the only correct way to say "affect"
Some editors object to impact as a verb meaning affect, though it is now common.
not be modified by words like "very"
Unique traditionally means one of a kind, so it cannot logically be "very unique."
informal; "all right" is the standard spelling
Many style guides still prefer "all right" in formal writing.
Data is traditionally the plural of datum, though "the data is" is now common.
Awesome originally meant inspiring awe; its use for "great" is a newer, casual meaning.
Terrific originally meant frightening, but its meaning has shifted to "excellent."
A speaker implies; a listener infers
A listener implies; a speaker infers
They mean exactly the same thing
To imply is to suggest; to infer is to draw a conclusion from what is suggested.
